info.title: Check one at a time
info.text:
Start at the first item.

Compare the item with the target.

Continue if it does not match.

Challenge: How many target comparisons find 27?

Three comparisons. With zero-based indexing, its index is 2.

info.title: Unsorted lists
info.text:
Linear search does not need sorted data.

Every item is still checked in sequence.

It also works on sorted lists.

Challenge: Why can linear search use an unsorted list?

It checks items directly and does not discard a half based on value order.

info.title: Unsuccessful searches
info.text:
A target may not be present.

Continue until the list is exhausted.

Then report not found.

Challenge: How many target comparisons are needed here?

Four, one for each item.

info.title: Read the code
info.text:
i tracks the current index.

found records whether a match exists.

Increase i after checking an item.

Challenge: What does data[i] == target test?

It compares the current list item with the search target.

info.title: Index versus value
info.text:
An index is a position, not the stored value.

Zero-based indexing starts at 0.

Report the form of result requested.

Challenge: State the value, index and comparison count for 9.

Value 9, index 2, and three target comparisons.

info.title: Best and worst cases
info.text:
First-item success needs one comparison.

Last-item success checks every item.

An absent target also checks every item.

Challenge: Why does a longer list worsen the worst case?

More items must be checked before a last-item match or not-found result.
